content:
sanjay: heads up — after the kernel selector roll last night i'm seeing a pattern where long-sequence tenants are blowing through the KV and causing short-seq tenants to get delayed or ejected from mini-batches. noticed lots of kv evictions and p99 spikes in the short-tail lanes.

maria: ugh. any profiling traces? sample request ids?

perf-bot: automatic profile summary for kernel=v3.14 | window=02:00-03:00 UTC:
 - overall token throughput: -6% vs baseline
 - KV hit rate (hot prefix): 74% -> 58% on high-load nodes
 - avg mini-batch size: 8 -> 12 for long tenants
 - p99 latency for seq<=64: 320ms -> 820ms
 - top callers: tenant-A (long, 30%), tenant-C (mixed, 20%)

oliver: suspects: kernel's batch-formation now favors length-concat heuristic, so long seqs accumulate into big batches and occupy GPU slots + KV gets churned. we probably need admission caps or a short-path reserve.

jen: idea: preemptive queue-sampling + token-budget floor for short lanes. instead of FIFO admit, sample heads with probability inversely proportional to expected token length (w/ smoothing). can keep a small reserved token pool for seq<=64 so they don't starve.

maria: +1. we should also tweak KV priming: avoid evicting prefixes seen in short seqs. maybe a bias: protect KV entries with high access frequency in last N requests weighted by tenant lane.

oliver: ran a local sim (micro-batcher sim) with 30% long traffic, 50% short, 20% medium. quick numbers (baseline -> with sampling+reserve):
 - short p99 latency: 780ms -> 210ms
 - long throughput delta: -3% (acceptible)
 - overall token cost: +1.2%
 - KV hit rate (short-prefixed): 59% -> 83%

sanjay: that's promising. what's the complexity of implementing sampling? can we do it in the admission fast path?

jen: implementation sketch:
```
# admission pseudocode
head = queue.peek()
if head.seq_len <= SHORT_THRESH:
  if short_reserve.tokens > head.tokens:
    admit(head)
  else:
    sample = rng() < short_bias_prob
    if sample: admit(head) else defer(head)
else:
  admit_long_policy(head)
```
Short_bias_prob computed from lane weights + exponential smoothing. reserve refills every 100ms based on token budget targets.

maria: telemetry we want for the canary: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 for short and long buckets, kv_hit_rate_by_prefix_size, mini_batch_size_distribution, evictions/sec, admission-defer-rate by lane. Also a "starvation_counter" for tenants blocked > X seconds.

perf-bot: created perf-check card: /cards/1749876543 with the above metrics; alert thresholds set for short p99 > 400ms or starvation_counter > 5 in 10m.

oliver: i'll push a canary branch with sampling + 1k-token short reserve. will instrument synthetic traffic and run for 4 hours.

maria: assigned: oliver (impl + sim), jen (algorithm tuning + math for budget refill), sanjay (canary rollout + watch). jen please post the math for reserve refill — want bounds for worst-case long influx.

jen: posted quick notes in thread: use leaky-bucket refill with refill_rate = short_target_tokens/sec, cap = short_target_tokens * 1.5. choose short_target_tokens so reserve covers median burst for 95th percentile short arrivals. i'll attach numbers to the card later.

sanjay: quick checklist before canary: 1) add tenant-weighted fairness metric to console (maria) 2) perf card + alerts (perf-bot done) 3) smoke test harness to simulate multi-tenant mix (oliver) 4) canary traffic schedule (i'll post). aim to deploy in next maintenance window.

maria: FYI — if this works we should consider making sampling a fallback policy in routing: when high eviction rate detected, bias toward short-path admission automatically.

perf-bot: smoke-run completed (oliver) — 1M requests simulated; no regressions in long throughput beyond -4%; short p99 improved 4x; no OOMs. Full logs on /artifacts/1749876543/sim.tar.gz

oliver: rolling into canary in staging now. will report back with first 30m telemetry.

sanjay: thanks all. keep messages concise in this thread. if anyone needs to spin up an ad-hoc meeting ping me. :thumbsup:
